summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recurrent UTIs due to urethral diverticulum was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake, along with severe pain and elevated blood pressure. IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain management with tramadol, Tylenol, and dilaudid were initiated. A central line was placed due to poor venous access. Hypertension was managed by increasing nifedipine to 90 mg daily. Blood cultures showed a single positive for coagulase-negative staph, deemed a contaminant; no ongoing antibiotics were given. Urinalysis showed pyuria but no growth, and no treatment was initiated. An EGD revealed mild gastric erythema but no ulcers or obstruction. Her symptoms improved, she advanced to a soft diet, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and plans for outpatient follow-up with primary care and gastroenterology, including a gastric emptying study and evaluation for a port and IV iron.
